title: Offering myself as tribute to the crowdfunding gods... (A case study in AI disclosure)
author: SpiritguideGames
selftext:
Hey friends\~ I've been a lurker in this community for a bit and I finally felt called to come out of hiding, as I'm now in active "test mode," you could say. 

I just **launched a Kickstarter campaign yesterday... and I am completely open about my AI usage.** It's disclosed in the special Kickstarter section for it and I also made a little FAQ just to address it. I launched a standalone teaser game on itch a couple of days ago with explicit disclosure. And my Steam page, also offering disclosure, has been live for a couple months now. 

Basically, **I see myself as a guinea pig** right now, testing the waters of how far I can go with an eventually-commercial game openly disclosing AI assets, and wanted to share what I've experienced so far, for anyone feeling apprehensive about doing the same. 

I've only seen a few Kickstarter campaigns openly disclosing AI usage so far, and none of them have funded. (If you have any examples, I'd love to see them!) 

So far, it hasn't been the most promising for me either, honestly. I expect people will come around to it more and more over time, but for now, I've been getting a lot of kickback. Especially given my game is primarily a visual novel and I'm still using some AI placeholder assets for the visuals (I know, I indulge in black magicks like that.)

Marketing, which I usually enjoy (don't judge, I'm weird!), has been a slog because most of the time, when reaching out to press, other devs for cross promo, etc., if I get any response at all, it seems to be just so people can express their disdain for my AI usage. That said, I can't honestly say why others don't respond. In some cases, I imagine the AI is part of it, in others cases, not. 

Alas, it's not all doom and gloom though! My Kickstarter, at this point, has raised about 8k euros, yay! Most of the backers seem to be people I already know through my business or have otherwise established trust with in some way, however. There aren't a ton of backers yet, but the people that do back tend to pledge a lot! 

My itch game has also been doing well (imo at least?). It's gotten about 100 downloads in just a few days. And about 1 in 10 people have submitted my feedback form. So far, that feedback has been overwhelmingly positive actually, woo! That said, this game uses very few AI visuals and the emphasis is on the writing, which I do entirely myself. 

**So, in short, what I've learned so far: trust goes a long way.** And I suspect, if you're gonna sell a game using an openly disclosed AI workflow, it's important to establish trust with your audience, however you feel called to do that. Also, people hate AI visuals. Like, a lot. And once they identify AI in one area of your project, they may just start seeing it it areas where it isn't.  

If you want to follow me on this roller coaster, here's my linkage:

[Kickstarter](https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/spiritguidegames/dragon-soul-awakening)

[Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5034110/Dragon_Soul_Awakening/)

[Free itch.io game](https://spiritguide-games.itch.io/shadowstarter)

I share this not as promo but for anyone curious to see *how* I disclose my AI usage. I was super curious about that when I was prepping for my Steam page and Kickstarter and it's interesting for me to see how different people handle and word it. 

I'd love to hear from other devs who are also openly disclosing AI in your workflow, especially for commercial projects! Cause, I mean, it can be rough out there? What has your experience been like? And have you tried crowdfunding? 🙈 

In any case, hope this helps! Keep on keeping\~

comments.author: -FlyingPenguin-
comments.body:
This is awesome! As of this comment, you have a lot of backing already. This gives me motivation for my project. Not sure if ill go crowdfunding route, but it sure is promising seeing your progress.

I am worried when I start marketing what that will look like. The AI hate is real.
